seen.where: DECODE R9263 = BL Cotton MS Caligula C V f. 78r-v, both images fetched with decode_fetch.py into scratch space (not in repo); Planta 1802 item 229 OCR https://archive.org/download/gri_33125005958521/gri_33125005958521_djvu.txt
seen.extent: One letter, 2 pages (f. 78r-v), French, headed 'From the Bishop of Glasgo to his brother, the first part. The rest to the Qu. of Scotte', 1575.
seen.cipher: f. 78r opens with four lines of cipher signs above the clear French body, which carries nomenclature signs and English marginal glosses ('forty dayes', 'monthe'); f. 78v ends with a written alphabet key (a-z signs) and a signs-for-mille line. So the leaf shows clear text, glosses and a key, not a bare cipher.

prior_art.decode: DECODE R9263 status Decrypted, inline cleartext yes; also R3824 (SP53/10, James Beaton to Andre Beaton 1575-77, Decrypted). known.py on Beaton Glasgow 1575 gave no hit in the harvested dump beyond R9263.
prior_art.tomokiyo: Cryptiana 2024/07 reconstructed ciphers related to Mary lists Beaton ciphers reconstructed by Bishop Kyle; DECODE note on R3824 gives the key on the next folio.
prior_art.lasry: Cryptologia 2023 (Lasry, Biermann, Tomokiyo) covers Mary-Beaton ciphers from 1576; no specific 1575 f. 78 reading found.
prior_art.edition: Planta 1802 item 229 calls it 'a cypher not deciphered'; no edition found that prints this letter.
prior_art.literature: Searches (Archbishop of Glasgow 1575 brother cipher Caligula C V; Beaton cipher 1575) found only BL catalogue, DECODE and the MB-cipher papers.

932.key_check: The alphabet key is written on f. 78v itself, and DECODE keys R3825/R4000 exist for the same sender; the body is largely clear French so the key was only inspected, not run.
932.key_in_volume: Written alphabet and nomenclature signs on Caligula C V f. 78v.
932.duplicates: Same document as DECODE R9263 (Caligula C V f. 78); Planta's item 229 of Caligula C III is this letter by wording and date. No catalogue entry or target.
932.closed: The leaf (DECODE R9263 images seen) is mostly clear French with a few nomenclature signs, English marginal glosses and an alphabet key on f. 78v, and DECODE lists it as Decrypted; only the four-line cipher header on f. 78r shows no plaintext beside it.
